scenario.title: Reusable plans and case definitions
situations: A user wants the same acceptance checks on many changes.
One change needs a one-off case.
A saved plan is edited after an item has already started.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Plan, attachment and snapshot documentation was inspected; detailed materialize/rematerialize behavior needs implementation-specific reconciliation before publication.
Verify current docs agree on newly added cases, frozen admitted copies and plan currency; do not infer mutation semantics from a simplified diagram.
Command nodes, when present, were checked with installed CLI --help only; this proves parser/help availability, not serving-control-plane capability or successful execution.

lessons.title: Understand the reusable layer
lessons.when: When the same acceptance checks should apply repeatedly, or the user opens QA Plans to create/attach a plan.
lessons.need: A plan is an ordered set of case definitions; each case has a stable key, method, instructions and expected result. Attach a plan to a project default or one item when its checks must gate work.
lessons.surface: QA Plans tab; plan authoring/attachment; project command registration
lessons.gap: Public QA introduces tabs then jumps into binding commands. Review question: should a short worked method/case/plan example replace that conceptual gap?

lessons.title: Snapshots protect running work
lessons.when: When editing a plan that already has attached/materialized requirements or an execution in progress.
lessons.need: Attachment/materialization turns definitions into subject-bound requirements. Later plan edits do not silently rewrite frozen execution or old evidence; explicit convergence and currency rules apply.
lessons.gap: Snapshot and convergence prose is split across public/private pages. Review question: should one canonical plans reference own it and plan-edit output link that owner?
surface_notes: Saved QA plan → materialized requirements: Reusable definitions and their subject-bound requirements are distinct records. Later edits follow explicit snapshot/currency rules rather than rewriting old proof.

lessons.title: A direct case is a valid small entrance
lessons.when: When one change needs a specific one-off proof that does not warrant a reusable plan.
lessons.need: A one-off method-backed requirement can target an item or deployment subject without inventing a reusable plan. Author with the actual claim, phase, transition and target.
lessons.surface: Explicit delivery-proof intake; case attachment authority
lessons.gap: Review question: should the diagram show direct-case authoring as a side entrance, avoiding an implied mandatory plan-creation step?
